_skillsAndMcps._note: Both kinds are classified, and there are slightly more skill repos than MCP servers. The 10 unclassified are the repositories that publish no description, or publish only "Agent superpowers" — they carry their axis-2 tag and nothing else, because tagging them from the vendor's name would be a guess dressed as a reading.

_theMarketRuledAgainstUS.what: `design` now has two parents. Ours, `design is a sub-domain of tool`, holds 990,000,001,000,000 shares. A pre-existing triple from the liquid-democracy project, `design is a sub-domain of governance`, holds 9,900,000,001,000,000 — ten times more, because it was created with a larger deposit. The stake rule therefore picks `governance`, which has no parent of its own, so the climb fails and `design` can produce no witness to our root.
_theMarketRuledAgainstUS.consequence: The 6 design tools are FINDABLE — a search descending `design` returns them, because search walks every authorising triple — but not PROVABLE. A delegation scoped on `tool` could not accept them. This is the generous-search / strict-verification asymmetry in docs/18 diverging for the first time on real data.
_theMarketRuledAgainstUS.whyItMatters: This is the mechanism working, not failing. The first genuine contest the domain market has had, it arbitrated against ARP, on ARP's own ontology, because somebody else paid more. A design where that could not happen would be the owner rule with extra steps.
theThreeOptions: Deposit on `design is a sub-domain of tool` until it exceeds 9.9e15 shares — roughly 0.018 more tTRUST. Outbidding, which is the sanctioned move.
Accept that `design` belongs to the other tree and pick a different word for ours.
Leave it. The tools are findable and only the witness is missing, and no delegation exists yet to need one.

_theReadingRule.what: ARP's tree is the set of hierarchy triples the attestor holds a position on, with shares > 0. The user's own formulation, 2026-10-28: « on crée ou on se positionne (on se positionne aussi quand on crée) et ça nous permet de faire le scope des domaines existants dans ARP ».
_theReadingRule.measured: The predicate carries 60 triples on 13579. The attestor has a position on 17 of them after the card-payment retirement. Reading from the positions returns those 17 and nothing else — no filtering logic, no ranking, no governance, no rehearsal nodes.
_theReadingRule.createIsBack: Creating a term with assets = cost + minDeposit leaves the creator one position, so creating and backing are the same act. Creating with assets = cost alone leaves ZERO positions, so such a term is on the chain and NOT in the tree (ADR 0053).
_theReadingRule.editable: Both directions, without the graph changing. Take a position and the triple joins the tree; redeem it and the triple leaves. The triple itself is permanent — what changes is whether OUR reading contains it.
_theReadingRule.whatWasDropped: The share auction. An earlier version ranked parents by total shares from everybody, which made the tree a function of money globally and handed `design` to another project's `governance` edge because it was funded 10x harder. That was the market idea applied where it does not belong; the user cut it (« tout n'a pas besoin d'être une market »). A separate ARP hierarchy predicate was also planned and then cancelled — the attestor filter makes it unnecessary, so it cost nothing.
twoGotchas: positions.account_id is CHECKSUMMED while atoms.creator_id is lowercase. A lowercase filter returns zero rows, which reads as 'nobody staked' rather than as a bad query.

A fully redeemed position leaves its row behind with shares: "0" instead of being removed. Without `shares: {_gt: "0"}` the retired triple stayed in the tree and the edit mechanism silently did nothing.
_theReadingRule.tagsAreNotFiltered: SUPERSEDED 2026-10-28, same day, by the user's question: « les has tag sont lues ouvertement mais alors n'importe qui peut mettre une has tag et créer de faux trucs non ? » — yes, for the price of one triple. The reasoning behind reading them openly was that other people's claims are the content ARP surfaces. True of claims, false of filing: a tag is an index entry, and an index anybody can write into is not an index. It also left the boundary inconsistent — the hierarchy was attestor-scoped so nobody could move `card` out from under `payment`, while anyone could hang anything under `card`. A locked door beside an open window.

attestorScoped: the hierarchy — it is the index
the has tag filings — they are the index
openToEveryone: positions and counter-triples — they are the market
theBoundaryNow.theLine: The index is curated, the opinions are open. A stable filing system is what makes the opinions comparable.
theBoundaryNow.itSilencesNobody: Disagreement with a filing is a deposit on its counter-triple, which every triple is born with. A different filing is a tag under a different attestor. `tag_source: 'any'` on arp_find_tools returns every filing with `tagged_by_arp` per row, so nothing is hidden.
theBoundaryNow.measuredExposure: 97 `has tag` triples point at ARP's 53 tool atoms on 13579 and all 97 carry an ARP position. Zero come from anywhere else, so this was latent and not live — it goes live the first time somebody else uses the registry.

whoChooses.decided: NOT the caller. The user, 2026-10-28: « je ne veux pas que ce soit modulable par un agent ou un mcp ou n'importe quoi, c'est le filet de sécurité du classement des info ».
whoChooses.why: `has tag` and the hierarchy are permissionless to WRITE, so the only thing separating ARP's index from anything anybody published is which positions it is read through. A caller that can pass its own attestor — or ask for none — can make the index say whatever it likes, and a curated index then guarantees nothing.
whoChooses.shape: The attestor is a property of the NODE (`ARP_DOMAIN_ATTESTOR`, falling back to `AGENT_ADDRESS`), set once at load. Anybody wanting a different index runs a node with a different attestor. `arp_find_tools` has no attestor parameter; the response still echoes `domain_attestor`, because the index is a reading and a reader must never have to guess whose.
whoChooses.aWrongTurnAndItLastedOneTurn: An earlier version took `attestor` from the arguments and offered `any`. It was reverted the same session, on the user's objection, before anything depended on it.
threeHolesFoundWhileClosingIt: A node with NO attestor fell back to reading the hierarchy unfiltered — the exact failure the design exists to prevent, and silent: a search returning more rows looks like a better answer, not like a missing guard rail. It now refuses the search.

An EMPTY string passed the `??` guard, because an empty string is not nullish. The query then ran with account_id: "" and every domain came back empty, which reads as "this domain has nothing in it". Blank is now treated as unset.

A LOWERCASE address passed the shape check and matched nothing, because positions.account_id is checksummed. It is now normalised with viem's getAddress rather than refused — verified: configuring the lowercase form returns the 6 design tools and echoes the checksummed address.
whoChooses.andOneCrash: The malformed-address branch called `log`, which is declared further down the file, so it threw a ReferenceError at module load and took the whole server down before it could serve anything. `console.error` instead — stderr is the right stream in both transports, since on stdio stdout is the protocol.
